body:
```suggestion
			Monitor output is formatted as a percentage. Submitted values should represent the percentage directly rather than a fraction, e.g. [code]100.0[/code] for [code]100.00%[/code].
```

Also, it might be worth considering whether it's better to submit it as a fraction instead (i.e. multiply by 100 in the backend). This way, you can do things like `number_of_alive_enemies / float(number_of_enemies)` and submit this as a custom performance monitor directly, without needing to multiply it yourself.

Time is already sent in seconds, presumably for a similar reason (and because Godot APIs generally reason in seconds unless integer values are a must-have).

My primary use case right now for these custom debug monitors is displaying performance metrics provided by the Meta Quest, many of which are provided in a percentage format that works with the above description.

This is a super minor thing, I'd personally probably put the implementation here in the header and mark it with `inline`. With LTO, it may not matter anyway, but as a purely internal class, we probably do want this getter to be inlined
I guess using a `TypedArray` here matches `get_custom_monitor_names()`, so this is probably fine. `Vector<int>` would be a somewhat faster and more compact data type for this
